applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) depicts seven (7) mitigation trees (marked 'M' designation) plotted with their trunk centers positioned directly at the overhead electric (OHE) line running along the southern property boundary. Vision analysis confirmed these tree symbols intersect the OHE utility line with zero (0) feet lateral distance measured. Two utility pole symbols (circles with crosses) are shown at the western and eastern ends of this OHE line. Trees are shown directly adjacent to or overlapping these pole locations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 prohibits trees within 10 lateral feet of any electric utility pole (measured from trunk center to pole). The landscape plan shows trees with trunk centers plotted at approximately 0 feet from the utility line where poles are located, which is well within the 10-foot prohibited zone. This represents a direct violation of the pole clearance requirement. The vision tool's examination of the plan found no dimension callouts that would indicate these trees are actually set back to compliant distances.
findings.comment: Seven mitigation trees are shown with trunk centers plotted directly on the overhead electric line where utility poles are located, placing them within the prohibited 10-foot clearance zone from utility poles.

applicableAreas: Throughout site near electrical infrastructure, particularly transformer pads and pull boxes
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows four transformer pads and eight+ pull boxes (underground electric equipment) distributed throughout the site. Vision analysis of Sheet 21 noted 'significant overlap' between these underground electrical infrastructure locations and existing tree canopy zones shown on the electrical plan. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) is being coordinated to add 20 proposed trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) plus shrubs and groundcover. Sheet 37 (Landscape Details) provides standard tree planting specifications but contains no root barrier specifications or references. Examination of all landscape sheets (31, 35, 37) reveals NO documentation of required root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) for any trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires root barriers for trees proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment: 'minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment.' Sheet 21 shows multiple transformer pads and pull boxes with tree canopy overlaps. The landscape plan (Sheet 31) provides no callouts, detail references, or notes specifying root barrier requirements for any of the 20 proposed trees or existing trees. Without root barrier documentation on the landscape and detail sheets, compliance with this requirement cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Trees are proposed and existing trees are shown near underground electrical transformer pads and pull boxes. No root barrier specifications (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are documented on the landscape plan or landscape detail sheets for any trees within the 20-foot protection zone.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows seven trees positioned along the OHE line with only the 'M' (mitigation tree) functional designation in the legend. While Sheet 35 provides a plant schedule listing four tree species to be planted (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), the specific species of each of the seven trees shown on the OHE line cannot be determined from the landscape plan. The plant schedule symbols are defined in Sheet 35 but are not callout-labeled on the landscape drawing to identify which species corresponds to each tree location.
findings.reasoning: Per the grouping's Reviewer Convention and common violation patterns (species misidentification), trees planted near electric facilities must be positively identified by species so their utility-compatibility status can be verified against ECM Appendix F. The landscape plan fails to provide species identification for the specific trees shown near the OHE line, making it impossible to verify whether they meet utility-compatible requirements or comply with size restrictions.
findings.comment: The plant legend on the landscape plan identifies the seven OHE-line trees only by functional designation (M = mitigation tree) without specifying species. Specific species must be identified for electric utility clearance verification.

applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: Comprehensive visual examination of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows no dimension lines, measurement arrows, or numerical distance callouts between any proposed trees and the overhead electric (OHE) line or utility poles. A detailed scan of the entire sheet confirmed absence of: (1) dimension lines between tree symbols and utility infrastructure, (2) written notes specifying clearances, (3) references to utility clearance requirements, or (4) any measurements related to tree-utility separation. The plan shows the OHE line and tree locations but provides no quantitative clearance verification.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires clearances measured as lateral distance from tree trunk center to the outside conductor. Measurement methodology must be documented on plans to verify compliance. The landscape plan shows trees at the OHE line but provides zero dimensional information. Without clearance dimensions, it is impossible to determine whether trees meet the required distances (15 feet for distribution clearance zones, 10 feet from poles). The absence of any measurement callouts is itself a deficiency.
findings.comment: No clearance dimensions, measurement lines, or distance callouts are shown on the landscape plan between trees and the overhead electric line or utility poles, preventing verification of compliance with minimum clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Overhead electric facilities throughout site, specifically southern OHE line
findings.observation: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) displays trees as circular symbols with inner trunk-center points and larger outer circles representing canopy extent. No dimension lines originate from tree trunk centers (the inner circle points representing planting locations). Where tree-utility distances appear to be dimensioned at all (which they are not), any measurement endpoints would be at the canopy edge rather than the planting trunk location. Vision analysis confirmed no measurements of any kind are shown on the plan.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 specifies that clearances must be measured from the tree trunk center (planting location), not from the projected canopy edge. The measurement methodology is critical because measuring from canopy edge significantly underestimates the distance available to utilities. The plan fails on two counts: (1) it provides no measurements at all, and (2) the tree symbols do not include dimension lines that would clarify measurement origin points (trunk vs. canopy).
findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are provided from tree trunk centers (planting locations) to utility conductors. The large canopy circles shown for each tree could be misinterpreted as measurement origins if any dimensions were present.

applicableAreas: Overhead electric line (OHE) along southern property boundary
findings.observation: Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) does show the overhead electric (OHE) line and seven proposed trees in visual proximity. However, the plan lacks any clearance verification information: no dimension callouts, no written notes specifying distances or compliance status, no reference to conductor locations for measurement origin, and no identification of the specific tree species for those trees near the OHE line. While trees and utilities are graphically shown together, clearance verification is impossible due to the complete absence of dimensional or specification information required to confirm compliance.
findings.reasoning: The grouping specifies that trees must be 'shown on landscape plan in relation to overhead electric facilities, preventing clearance verification.' The intent of this requirement is to ensure viewers can verify that the spatial relationship satisfies clearance requirements. Although trees and OHE are displayed on the same drawing, the lack of any dimension, note, or specification information prevents any meaningful verification. Showing trees and utilities on the same sheet without clearance documentation is insufficient for code compliance verification.
findings.comment: Trees are shown on the landscape plan in proximity to the overhead electric line, but without clearance dimensions, distance callouts, or specification notes, clearance verification is prevented.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along OHE line where seven trees are plotted
findings.observation: Seven mitigation trees are shown on Sheet 31 with trunk centers positioned at approximately zero (0) feet lateral distance from the overhead electric (OHE) line. This placement is clearly within the restricted clearance zone (< 15 feet from distribution conductors, < 10 feet from utility poles). No documentation of Austin Energy written approval is present on the landscape plan, electrical plan, site notes, or in the supplementary documents (no letters or approval certificates are referenced or attached). The plans propose trees in prohibited zones with no evidence of required variance authorization.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.4 states that 'Variations to planting distances and species identified as utility-compatible in ECM Appendix F require explicit written approval from Austin Energy.' Trees proposed within prohibited zones (< 15 feet distribution, < 10 feet poles) must include documented Austin Energy approval. The site plan shows no such approval. Without documented authorization, the proposed tree locations violate the clearance requirements.
findings.comment: Trees are proposed at zero feet from the overhead electric line in direct violation of minimum clearance requirements. No documented written approval from Austin Energy is present on the plans to authorize this variance.
